engine_shadow_ledger.basis_note: every row here is scored from the committee vote the board froze before first pitch. No engine pick is scored any other way, so the cut is one kind of evidence throughout — the two bases `pick_confidence` defines are never mixed inside one table.

streaks.note: pushes are neutral — they neither extend nor break a streak. `site` runs over the SAME served picks record.headline counts, straight through the engine changeover; each analyst's runs over that analyst's own v2 reads, which are a different and much larger population — the two are never summed.

decided_live.rule: a totals bet is DECIDED the instant the runs scored exceed the line it was served at: the over has won and the under has lost, and runs never come off the board. Only the over-CLINCH can be known early — so an under IS graded early, as a LOSS, and what can never be known before the final is an under WINNING.
decided_live.confirmation: a verdict is written only after 2 separate reads of the feed show the line passed, with no runs coming off the board between them. One read is evidence, not a verdict; a run count that goes backwards is proof one read was false and nothing is written.
decided_live.corrections: the ledger is never rewritten, but the PUBLISHED record prefers the settled final wherever a final disagrees with an early verdict, and marks the row. A correction is visible, never silent.
decided_live.names_no_sides: deliberately no per-game side, line or result here: a bet can die while its game is still being played, and its card is still locked for a signed-out reader. The counts move the record honestly without handing anyone the pick.
decided_live.write_once: an early grade is written once, with the runs and the clock reading at the instant the bet died, and that LEDGER ROW is never rewritten — it is the honest record of what a reader was shown. It does not outrank the settled final: where a final disagrees, the final is what the record publishes and the row is marked corrected. See `corrections`.

reconciliation.note: an early verdict and the final verdict must be identical; a disagreement is a bug in the predicate, never a reason to restate a written row.

surfaces.note: record.headline is the DiamondEdge record. Every other stream/strategy record in this payload is a RESEARCH variant: still graded, still honest, still published — and not a product record. Nothing here ranks or features them.

copy_policy.rule: story / news / desk copy reads ONLY the story_safe blocks. The research_only blocks keep every measurement, sample and interval they have always carried — they are for the Research surface, which reframes a null as 'we tested this, the market prices it, so we bet elsewhere'. No story-safe field may carry null-finding language, and nothing in the payload ranks a research block onto the record or desk surfaces: record.headline is the only product record.

adaptive_selector_replay.label: Selector replay — NOT a track record
adaptive_selector_replay.why_not_the_record: these picks were never served. They are what the current selector says it would have chosen on days the champion/model engine was actually on the board. Judging the selector: useful. Quoting it as a record: an advertisement.

diagnostics.note: measurements kept for judging the engines. Nothing here is a track record and nothing here is ever summed into record.headline.

display_layer.what: the adaptive desk — one strategy locked per date from strictly-prior graded history, applied to that date's games. This is the board and the headline record.

supplemental.what: a pick Leon adds by hand from the expanded engine (v2, in shadow), on a game the desk did NOT pick, before first pitch. It FILLS, it never overrides: a supplemental row for a game that already has a served pick, or for a game that has started, is REFUSED and the refusal is published.
supplemental.write_once: admitted once, frozen at that instant into state/supplemental_served.jsonl, replayed from there on every later build, and hash-pinned with the rest of the archive
supplemental.counted: in record.headline, in the day's record and in record.by_source, on its own source line — it was served pregame at a real price, so it is a real pick, and it is never blended into the desk's own line

withdrawal.what: Leon may SUPERSEDE a still-PREGAME served pick, so the board serves that game as a PASS instead. It is refused outright once the game is inside the pregame margin: a standing offer may be taken off the board, a live position may not.
withdrawal.never_an_edit: nothing is rewritten and nothing is deleted. The original row is archived verbatim in state/superseded_picks_<date>.jsonl with what superseded it, who authorised it and when — a second dated fact laid on top of the first, not a change to it
withdrawal.write_once: applied once, first application wins forever, and replayed clocklessly on every later build — a rebuild can no more resurrect a withdrawn pick than it can drop a served one
withdrawal.counted: in NO record. The game was never decided, so it leaves the day's denominator rather than entering it as a win or a loss — which is only honest because the gate refuses any withdrawal on a game that has started

archive_layer.note: The ARCHIVE layer holds every pick the older engines ever served. It is append-only and hash-pinned per day. It is NOT the board: since 2026-08-02 the board is the adaptive desk (the DISPLAY layer). The archive's job is to prove history was never rewritten.

copy.rule: story / news / desk copy reads ONLY the story_safe blocks. The research_only blocks keep every measurement, sample and interval they have always carried — they are for the Research surface, which reframes a null as 'we tested this, the market prices it, so we bet elsewhere'. No story-safe field may carry null-finding language, and nothing in the payload ranks a research block onto the record or desk surfaces: record.headline is the only product record.

policy.summary: ARCHIVE vs DISPLAY. The write-once served-pick stores are the ARCHIVE layer: append-only, immutable, hash-pinned, never the board. The adaptive desk is the DISPLAY layer: one strategy locked per date from strictly-prior history, and the only thing the site shows or counts. The two populations disagree by design from 2026-08-02; each is reconciled against its OWN ledger, never against the other.

backtest.window: 2026-03-25..2026-07-23 (walk-forward rows only; one game per day-game, best-EV wall; graded vs settled finals at the row's own executable price)
backtest.note: BACKTEST (would-have) record — NOT a served record. The served expanded-band record accrues from EXPANDED_BAND_START under record.by_star_tier['2_expanded'], separately from core 2*.

expanded_band.note: served_record is the ONLY record the expanded band has earned live (starts 0-0-0 at activation); `backtest` is the labeled would-have measurement that justified the band. The two are never merged. DISPLAY (2026-07-25): expanded picks carry regular stars on the one ladder and are counted inside by_star_tier (each tier's includes_expanded_n says how many) — this block is the band's own separate grading, unchanged.

streaks.note: pushes are neutral — they neither extend nor break a streak

insights.basis: honest aggregates over the SAME one-per-game graded unified picks as record.overall — nothing re-graded, no new claims. equity_curve is CUMULATIVE (units_flat = 1u per pick at the row's own executable price; units_weighted = tier-ladder staked, expanded fills 0.5u); by_star_perf uses the current v3.3 display bands over all history; calibration_buckets compare the served side's model probability to the realized win rate (pushes excluded); streaks treat pushes as neutral.

spread_stream.label: Spread stream (run line)
spread_stream.what: The run-line (±1.5) side per game — a NEW stream, live from 2026-07-27, graded in public from day one, starting 0-0-0. Separate from the totals product in every record.

engine.model: residual_spread_v1 (rolling engine full-game spread cells — the same live engine that serves totals; direction only)
engine.basis: run-line stream, served as LEANS only: the direction is the live model's read of the run line, locked at first pitch and graded at the real locked price, in public, from day one. A lean is never a bet.
engine.upgrade_path: UPGRADE PATH: a future run-line engine that passes its margin fitness gate with a surviving arm and real economics can flip the stream to sim_pricing (P(cover) from a validated joint margin distribution, +EV gate at real per-side prices, max 2*). The 2026-07-27 DERIV_RUNLINE_MARGIN_REPORT verdict was BLOCKED (prereg K1: margin fitness gate failed — no home-field advantage in the engine; and every declared arm, including the no-sim control, lost to the de-vigged market on Brier), so lean_only stands. The flip is explicit and human-signed (state/spread_engine_mode.json) — never automatic, never regex-parsed off a research report.

spread_stream.note: GRADED LEAN LEDGER. Every stated run-line lean is locked at first pitch and graded against the final at the real locked price, in public, from the 2026-07-27 activation forward. A lean carries no units, and this ledger is never added to, or compared against, the totals record.
spread_stream.separation: this record counts ONLY stream-stamped run-line rows graded on/after 2026-07-27; it never contains a totals row, and no totals record (overall, by_strategy, live_record, champion) ever contains a spread row — selftested in spread_stream, daily_cycle and unified_model

price_validity.why: run-line results before 2026-07-31 were graded from best-price columns written before the price-validity rule landed. Their two-sided prices imply arbitrage that was never obtainable (5th-percentile overround 0.729), so the ROI and units on those rows are not a measurement of anything. W-L is unaffected; the money is.

sim_stream.label: Physical run simulator
sim_stream.what: A fully-physical Monte Carlo of the game — every plate appearance drawn from empirical base-out transition tables tilted to the two lineups, starters, bullpens, park, weather and umpire as of each decision wall (T-24h through T-1h, re-priced as inputs firm up, each wall written once), with home-field advantage on — priced into P(over the posted total). The lean that grades is the latest wall locked at first pitch. Shown for transparency: on full-game totals it statistically TIES the market (its median lands within ~0.02 runs of the posted line; blend-vs-market p=0.28), so it is a tracked voice, never a bet.

engine.model: physical Monte Carlo run simulator (v4/models/forecast/monte_carlo_sim s1-s9; HFA ON; 20,000 sims/game, re-priced at every decision wall)
engine.decision_point: every wall T-24h/T-12h/T-6h/T-3h/T-1h — write-once per wall; the latest wall locked at first pitch is what grades

calibration.recipe: walk-forward mean map E[runs] = a + b*mu_raw, last expanding-window fold (prior months only)

evidence.engine_fitness: ENGINE_FIT_PASS (s5 gate 0): variance ratio and skew inside tolerance; the distributional shape is real
evidence.vs_market: primary arm (sim_blend) brier_gap +1.28e-04 vs the de-vigged market, day-clustered bootstrap p=0.279 over n=8412 — a statistical TIE; no declared arm beat the market
evidence.median_vs_line: the calibrated sim's MEDIAN lands within ~0.02 runs of the posted line on average — an independent physical model reproducing Vegas's number
evidence.hfa: s9 home-field module ON (fit on 2018-21 training seasons only)

engine.basis: physics simulator — an independent read that prices within a whisker of the market
engine.upgrade_path: UPGRADE PATH: if a future engine-vs-market report (v4/models/output/SIM_TOTALS_EDGE_REPORT.md) shows the simulator actually beating the de-vigged market on a declared, walk-forward, BH-controlled test, the stream may flip to a priced mode — and only via an explicit human-signed state file (state/sim_engine_mode.json) written after that report is read. The 2026-07 sim round's verdict was a TIE (primary arm brier_gap +1.28e-04, p=0.279; the market won or tied every declared arm), so transparent_voice stands. The flip is never automatic and never regex-parsed off a research report.

sim_stream.note: GRADED LEAN LEDGER. The simulator prices every game's posted total from a full physical simulation and states which side its probability implies; it re-prices at each decision wall as inputs firm up (T-24h through T-1h, every wall write-once, never revised), and the lean that grades is the LATEST wall locked at first pitch — one graded row per game, graded against the final in public, from the 2026-07-28 activation forward. A lean carries no units, and the engine's validated result is that it TIES the market. The record is never added to, or compared against, the totals or spread records.
sim_stream.separation: this record counts ONLY sim-stamped rows from the stream's own ledger (state/sim_graded.jsonl), graded on/after 2026-07-28; it never contains a row from the totals or spread ledgers, and no totals/spread record ever contains a simulator row — the simulator never writes the shared board or the shared graded ledger at all (selftested in sim_stream, daily_cycle and unified_model)

scout_stream.label: Simple-8 fundamentals model
scout_stream.what: Eight numbers a 1990s scout would recognise — both starters' ERAs, both teams' last-30-day batting averages, both bullpens' ERAs, the park's 3-year run factor and the game-time temperature — refit every morning on every settled game since 2022 and applied as an adjustment to the market's own probability at the T-3h wall. Shown for transparency: in the forecast round the de-vigged market edged this exact model (brier gap +1.96e-04, p=0.80, n=9,168), so it serves as a tracked voice, never a bet.

engine.model: simple-8 fundamentals residual model (fundamentals_baseline S1::residual; ridge-logistic on the logit(p_market) offset, lambda=300; walk-forward daily refit on T-3h rows; priced at EVERY wall T-24h/T-12h/T-6h/T-3h/T-1h from 2026-07-30 so no game is ever a no-read)
engine.wall_disclosure: coefficients are fit on T-3h rows (the frozen prereg recipe, unchanged); at earlier walls those same coefficients are applied to that wall's as-of inputs. Each row stamps wall_train_serve_match so the seam is visible per row. The pitching analyst is a tracked lean, never a bet — nothing here is staked.
engine.refit: expanding-window daily: predict_day(D) trains on every settled game with game_date < D (research store 2022-03-21..2026-07-04 + serve-era store 2026-07-06..)

evidence.vs_market: S1::residual (this exact 8-input offset recipe) brier_gap +1.96e-04 vs the de-vigged market, day-clustered bootstrap p=0.799 over n=9,168 dev games (2022-2026) — the market wins; no declared arm in the family beat it
evidence.family_verdict: all 6 declared fundamentals arms (S1/S2/R x standalone/residual) failed G1; economics never run (prereg forbids monetising a no-gain cell)
evidence.why_this_arm: S1::residual is the closest-to-market arm of the family and the one Leon named for the desk: 8 inputs, interpretable, honest

engine.basis: simple-8 fundamentals model — a classic eight-stat read, tracked against the market
engine.upgrade_path: UPGRADE PATH: if a future engine-vs-market report (v4/models/output/SCOUT_TOTALS_EDGE_REPORT.md) shows this model actually beating the de-vigged market on a declared, walk-forward, BH-controlled test, the stream may flip to a priced mode — and only via an explicit human-signed state file (state/scout_engine_mode.json) written after that report is read. The fundamentals round's verdict was an honest null (S1::residual brier_gap +1.96e-04, p=0.799 — the market won every declared arm), so transparent_voice stands. The flip is never automatic and never regex-parsed off a research report.

scout_stream.note: GRADED LEAN LEDGER. The pitching analyst prices every game's posted total from eight classic fundamentals and states which side its probability implies; each stated lean is locked when it is computed at the T-3h wall (write-once) and graded against the final in public, from the 2026-07-30 activation forward. A lean carries no units and no stars — a tracked voice, graded in the open. The record is never added to, or compared against, the totals or spread records.
scout_stream.separation: this record counts ONLY scout-stamped rows from the stream's own ledger (state/scout_graded.jsonl), graded on/after 2026-07-30; it never contains a row from the totals, spread or simulator ledgers, and no other record ever contains a scout row — the stream never writes the shared board or the shared graded ledger at all (selftested here and in unified_model)

unified.label: The DiamondEdge Pick
unified.what: The one pick we actually serve on this game: the champion's play if it has one, otherwise the model's best playable lean, otherwise a PASS.
unified.basis: POPULATION: every (date, game_pk) where the served hybrid produced a graded pick — champion play if present, else the model's best playable lean — exactly one row per game. GRADING: the row's own settled result at the real executable per-side price it was served at, on the line locked at first pitch; pushes return the stake and leave the ROI denominator. HEADLINE COVERS: served picks from 2026-07-20 (the day the hybrid went live) forward only.
unified.note: This is the product. Everything else on this page is a component or a diagnostic. The pre-activation block is the same rule applied backwards over picks the champion and the model really made — the picks are real, the selection between them is a would-have, and part of it rests on the champion's rolling-origin backtest.

champion.label: Champion engine
champion.what: The champion engine's own totals play — its frozen pipeline plus the +EV gate at the real per-side price. It only speaks on games where its trigger fires; on every other game it has no view at all.

forward_paper_live.what: logged forward in the champion's paper ledger before first pitch

live_board.what: served live on the v4 board and graded that night

repaired_live_day.what: a live day whose board was unstable (2026-07-08 serving bug) and was reconstructed under the fixed pipeline

backtest.label: ROLLING-ORIGIN WALK-FORWARD BACKTEST — the champion's own pipeline replayed on an expanding window. Nothing was served or logged on these days.

rolling_origin_backtest.what: rolling-origin expanding-window WALK-FORWARD BACKTEST of the champion's own pipeline — nothing was served or logged on these days

combined_view.label: PUBLISHED COMBINED (live + reconstructed/backtest) — shown only because the older blocks report it. This is NOT a live record; do not quote it as one.

champion.basis: POPULATION: every game the champion engine itself rated PLAYABLE and that settled — one row per game (its highest-score playable wall). This is NOT the champion's published headline, which counts one row per game x STREAM at the last decision wall; the two populations are reconciled to a zero residual, and the reconciliation is checked on every build. GRADING: champion_v2's own graded ledger, untouched — gate at the median de-vig price, priced and settled at the best executable price at the same line. HEADLINE COVERS: forward paper ledger + live board from 2026-07-02 forward. The 2026-03-27..06-10 rolling-origin rows are a WALK-FORWARD BACKTEST and are reported separately.
champion.note: The champion only speaks when its trigger fires; on most games it has no view at all, which is not a PASS. Read the live number and the backtest number separately — they are far apart, and the live sample is small.

model_v4.label: V4 model grid
model_v4.what: The v4 model grid's best playable totals lean on the game (the price gate at the real price, and a clear margin between our number and the market's).

archive_asof_wall.what: as-of-wall reconstruction of a day the board WAS live (leak-safe two-pass recipe, hash-asserted); not a fresh backtest, but not the served row byte-for-byte either

live_ledger.what: the v4 grid's own live graded ledger — the rows the board served

model_v4.basis: POPULATION: every game where the v4 model grid had a playable totals row that settled — one row per game (core playable preferred over an expanded-band row, then highest score). This DELIBERATELY INCLUDES games the champion also played, which record.by_source.model does NOT: by_source counts only the games the model FILLED after the champion passed, so the two numbers differ and neither is wrong. GRADING: the grid's own graded rows — as-of-wall archive where a day has one, else the live graded ledger — at each row's real executable per-side price. HEADLINE COVERS: 2026-07-06 forward (the first day the grid's live ledger graded anything).
model_v4.note: The grid rates every game, so it has a view on almost everything. Most of those views are PASSes; the bet set is the playable rows only. Its record here is bigger than record.by_source.model because this counts every game it played, not only the ones it filled.

expanded_band.label: Expanded band
expanded_band.what: The narrow near-miss band: the full price gate cleared but our number and the market's are only narrowly apart. Live from 2026-07-24, stakes 0.5u, graded on its own.

live_ledger.what: the v4 grid's own live graded ledger — the rows the board served

expanded_band.note: One or two live picks is not a record. The band was activated on a measured backtest and is being watched, not proven. It is a subset of the model grid — never add it to model_v4.

simulator.basis: POPULATION: every game the physical simulator priced from its 2026-07-28 activation forward — ONE graded row per game. The sim re-prices at each decision wall as inputs firm up (T-24h through T-1h from 2026-07-30; T-3h only before that), every wall write-once, and the row that grades is the LATEST wall locked at first pitch (earlier walls settle 'superseded', kept for audit, never counted). Sim-stamped rows from the stream's OWN ledger only. GRADING: the stated lean (the side implied by the sim's P(over) vs the market's) graded against the settled final at the LOCKED posted line, overnight, append-only. A LEAN LEDGER: every stated lean locks at first pitch and grades in public at the real locked line; no units are staked, is_bet is false on every row, and stars are hard-capped at 1*. HEADLINE COVERS: 2026-07-28 forward only — the stream starts 0-0-0 and the headline counts only what it has done live; the sim round's backtest (a statistical TIE with the market) is evidence about the engine.
simulator.note: A fully-physical model of baseball whose median independently lands on Vegas's number — shown for transparency, graded in public. GRADED LEAN LEDGER. The simulator prices every game's posted total from a full physical simulation and states which side its probability implies; it re-prices at each decision wall as inputs firm up (T-24h through T-1h, every wall write-once, never revised), and the lean that grades is the LATEST wall locked at first pitch — one graded row per game, graded against the final in public, from the 2026-07-28 activation forward. A lean carries no units, and the engine's validated result is that it TIES the market. The record is never added to, or compared against, the totals or spread records.

record.by_strategy_note: READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING STRATEGIES. (1) THEY OVERLAP: the same game appears in more than one stream — expanded_band is a strict SUBSET of model_v4, and unified is whichever of champion/model_v4 won that game. Their records are NOT additive: do not sum n, units or ROI across strategies, and do not read 'four strategies' as four independent bets. (2) NO POST-HOC PICKING: choosing whichever stream currently looks best is not a strategy — with four overlapping streams on a few dozen graded picks, one of them looks good by construction. The only number that ever described a real bankroll is the served unified pick from its activation date forward. (3) LIVE vs BACKTEST are kept apart on purpose: each strategy's headline n/W-L-P here is its LIVE-SERVED picks only; reconstructed / walk-forward / would-have measurements sit in `backtest`, are labeled, and are never added to the live number. `combined_view` restates the union ONLY because the older published blocks (record.overall, record.by_source) report it — it is not a live record. (4) Sample sizes here are small. None of this is an edge claim.

vega.title: THE PRICE
vega.thesis: The number is the evidence, so I grade the market and nothing else: where it opened, how far it moved, how much the books disagree and what the two sides actually cost.

vega.formula: logit(p_over) = logit(p_market) + -0.0542 +0.0000*z[line_move] +0.0000*z[move_pace] -0.0030*z[time_since_move] +0.1270*z[book_disagreement] -0.0494*z[price_dispersion] +0.0169*z[sharp_gap] +0.0263*z[n_books] -0.0664*z[stale_gap]   ;   side = over if p_over > p_market else under

patterns.honest_note: HOW A PATTERN EARNS ITS PLACE. Every row carries its n and an EXACT binomial (Clopper-Pearson) 95% interval, and a row is named a FINDING only after it survives a Benjamini-Hochberg pass across the entire rendered family — a deliberately high bar, so what gets named has earned it. REPOINTED 2026-07-31: The four sides come from the re-architected v2 analysts (analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date, the published chief contract) — the pitching analyst the arms, the hitting analyst the bats, the conditions analyst the conditions, the price analyst the price — not from the four ledgers of the previous analysts, which no longer exist. THE BUCKETS MOVED AND THAT IS NOT A RESULT: The re-architecture decorrelated the four deliberately, so they disagree far more (side agreement fell from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57) and all sixteen configurations now occur where most previously never did. Different population is not better or worse performance. The corpus restarts at 2026-07-01, the day after the training fence of 2026-06-30, so it is genuinely out of sample, and it deepens every night. The two eras are computed and shown separately and are NEVER summed: `reconstructed_era` is the July slate priced after the fact by models fitted before it, `live_era` is reads served before the games were played. Betting confidence remains solely the champion EV gate + the star system — nothing in this table gates, sizes or creates a bet.

desk_calls.note: THE DESK'S CALLS, GRADED IN THEIR OWN LEDGER. This is NOT a betting record and must never be summed with one, shown beside one as a comparison, or described in units: a call has no price and no stake, so it has no ROI. It counts one row per game — the desk's view at the most informed wall it reached — and it exists to answer one question the product could not previously ask: when the desk says something, is it right? A CALL IS NOT A BET. This is the desk's directional view on the game — what it actually thinks — built from the four analysts' own reads, equal-weighted. It is NEVER staked, it NEVER enters games[].pick, it is never counted in the product record, and it cannot be sized. Whether we are betting this game is a separate question with a separate answer, at `we_are_betting` / `bet_action`, decided by the price gate alone and unchanged by anything here. The graded product remains games[].pick and only games[].pick; the desk's calls are graded in their own ledger, separately, from 2026-08-01.
desk_calls.contract: THE DESK-CALL CONTRACT (2026-08-01). WHAT IT IS: a directional view on EVERY game — side, conviction, a probability and a one-line argument — built from the four analysts' own reads, equal-weighted (the measured house position: desk_fit's walk-forward refused a fitted combiner). SERVED AT games[].diamondedge.desk_call. WHAT IT IS NOT: A CALL IS NOT A BET. Whether we are betting a game is decided by the price gate alone and is served, unchanged, at games[].diamondedge.action (PLAY / LEAN / AVOID, where AVOID still means and only means that no bet was served) and at games[].pick. Every call row hard-stamps is_bet=False, staked=False, stake_units=None, playable=False, suggested_units=None, take=False, stars=None and pick_side=None, and those stamps are re-asserted on every write and every read; the module may write only its own three stores and refuses every served board and product ledger by name. THE VOCABULARY, and a reader can never mistake one axis for the other: `desk_call.call` is the CALL (STRONG/CLEAR/SLIGHT + OVER/UNDER), `desk_call.state` fuses both axes (CALL_AND_PLAY / CALL_AND_LEAN / CALL_NO_BET / CALL_NO_GAME / PENDING), `we_are_betting` is the bet in one boolean, and `why_no_bet` names the reason when it is false. GRADING: the graded product remains games[].pick and ONLY games[].pick. The desk's calls are graded in their own append-only ledger, one row per game at its most informed wall, from 2026-08-01, with no units and no ROI because a call has no price.

voice.name: The Pitcher's Park, the Rested Arm and the Closer Up
paragraphs: This one lives on the ballpark, the starting pitching, and the bullpens. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds another of our models reading the over, a ballpark that has been taking runs away, and a visiting starter working on extra rest. Another of our models reading the over is the ordinary case for the over. The rest of it is not: A ballpark that has been taking runs away and a visiting starter working on extra rest are what you would normally write down the other way, and wanting both at once is the whole idea. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst is not strongly on the under, the visiting closer available for the ninth, and the ballpark is the biggest thing setting this game's run environment. Same shape, mirrored — the visiting closer available for the ninth is the obvious part and the conditions analyst is not strongly on the under is the part that cuts against it.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Jul 22 to Aug 7) it played 174 of the 221 games it saw, and it went 125-46-3.

paragraphs: This one lives on the bullpens, the shape of the matchup, and our four analysts. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a home pen with nobody working back-to-back, the home starter is known and the home starter's walk rate is below 0.09, and both starters are known and the two starters' average strikeout rate is below 0.23. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: This is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst's P(over) is below 0.53, both starters are known and the two starters' gap in contact allowed (home minus away) is at least -0.03, and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is below 1. That side of it is the straightforward one.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Aug 4 to Aug 20) it played 180 of the 226 games it saw, and it went 120-51-9.

voice.name: The Pitcher's Park, the Rested Arm and the Closer Up
paragraphs: This one lives on the ballpark, the starting pitching, and the bullpens. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds another of our models reading the over, a ballpark that has been taking runs away, and a visiting starter working on extra rest. Another of our models reading the over is the ordinary case for the over. The rest of it is not: A ballpark that has been taking runs away and a visiting starter working on extra rest are what you would normally write down the other way, and wanting both at once is the whole idea. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst is not strongly on the under, the visiting closer available for the ninth, and the ballpark is the biggest thing setting this game's run environment. Same shape, mirrored — the visiting closer available for the ninth is the obvious part and the conditions analyst is not strongly on the under is the part that cuts against it.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Jul 22 to Aug 7) it played 174 of the 221 games it saw, and it went 125-46-3.

caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

The four sides sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points, printed beside each rate. What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. What each side earns from here is the forward record's to say, nightly and in public.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT, HELD TO A HARD BAR. Every night it re-fits, over the trailing 30 days, how each analyst's disagreement with the price has related to results — scored strictly WALK-FORWARD, fitted only on days before the day it is scored on — and holds the fit to two baselines at once: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are adopted only when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting is strictly clear of zero and the window carries enough reads to fit four weights; until they earn that, the desk weights its analysts equally and prints the numbers. The +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet.

forge_strategy.summary_line: Today's board is one rule. It came out of last night's search with the best win-minus-loss record over the window, and it was frozen before the first game. Over the 17 nights it was chosen on (2026-08-04 to 2026-08-20), this rule went 120-51-9.

paragraphs: This one lives on the bullpens, the shape of the matchup, and our four analysts. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a home pen with nobody working back-to-back, the home starter is known and the home starter's walk rate is below 0.09, and both starters are known and the two starters' average strikeout rate is below 0.23. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: This is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst's P(over) is below 0.53, both starters are known and the two starters' gap in contact allowed (home minus away) is at least -0.03, and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is below 1. That side of it is the straightforward one.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Aug 4 to Aug 20) it played 180 of the 226 games it saw, and it went 120-51-9.

source.no_longer_read: v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — the walk-forward reconstruction of the PREVIOUS four analysts (the price analyst the champion engine, the hitting analyst the v4 grid, the conditions analyst the simulator, the pitching analyst the simple-8 fundamentals). Those four were dismantled on 2026-07-31; a weight fitted on their behaviour is not a weight for the analysts it would be applied to. desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 434 games and 34 days the log-loss difference is -0.00032 (95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

The four sides sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points, printed beside each rate. What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. What each side earns from here is the forward record's to say, nightly and in public.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT, HELD TO A HARD BAR. Every night it re-fits, over the trailing 30 days, how each analyst's disagreement with the price has related to results — scored strictly WALK-FORWARD, fitted only on days before the day it is scored on — and holds the fit to two baselines at once: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are adopted only when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting is strictly clear of zero and the window carries enough reads to fit four weights; until they earn that, the desk weights its analysts equally and prints the numbers. The +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet.

coherence.note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 434 games and 34 days the log-loss difference is -0.00032 (95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

The four sides sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points, printed beside each rate. What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. What each side earns from here is the forward record's to say, nightly and in public.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT, HELD TO A HARD BAR. Every night it re-fits, over the trailing 30 days, how each analyst's disagreement with the price has related to results — scored strictly WALK-FORWARD, fitted only on days before the day it is scored on — and holds the fit to two baselines at once: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are adopted only when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting is strictly clear of zero and the window carries enough reads to fit four weights; until they earn that, the desk weights its analysts equally and prints the numbers. The +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet.

paragraphs: This one lives on the bullpens, the shape of the matchup, and our four analysts. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a home pen with nobody working back-to-back, the home starter is known and the home starter's walk rate is below 0.09, and both starters are known and the two starters' average strikeout rate is below 0.23. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: This is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst's P(over) is below 0.53, both starters are known and the two starters' gap in contact allowed (home minus away) is at least -0.03, and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is below 1. That side of it is the straightforward one.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Aug 4 to Aug 20) it played 180 of the 226 games it saw, and it went 120-51-9.

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 434 games and 34 days the log-loss difference is -0.00032 (95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025]). desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

The four sides sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points, printed beside each rate. What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. What each side earns from here is the forward record's to say, nightly and in public.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT, HELD TO A HARD BAR. Every night it re-fits, over the trailing 30 days, how each analyst's disagreement with the price has related to results — scored strictly WALK-FORWARD, fitted only on days before the day it is scored on — and holds the fit to two baselines at once: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are adopted only when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting is strictly clear of zero and the window carries enough reads to fit four weights; until they earn that, the desk weights its analysts equally and prints the numbers. The +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet.

paragraphs: This one lives on the bullpens, the shape of the matchup, and our four analysts. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a home pen with nobody working back-to-back, the home starter is known and the home starter's walk rate is below 0.09, and both starters are known and the two starters' average strikeout rate is below 0.23. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: This is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst's P(over) is below 0.53, both starters are known and the two starters' gap in contact allowed (home minus away) is at least -0.03, and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is below 1. That side of it is the straightforward one.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Aug 4 to Aug 20) it played 180 of the 226 games it saw, and it went 120-51-9.

What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

The four sides sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points, printed beside each rate. What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. What each side earns from here is the forward record's to say, nightly and in public.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT, HELD TO A HARD BAR. Every night it re-fits, over the trailing 30 days, how each analyst's disagreement with the price has related to results — scored strictly WALK-FORWARD, fitted only on days before the day it is scored on — and holds the fit to two baselines at once: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are adopted only when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting is strictly clear of zero and the window carries enough reads to fit four weights; until they earn that, the desk weights its analysts equally and prints the numbers. The +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet.

desk_combined.note: the desk's weighted combination of the four analysts' disagreement with the price. DISPLAY ONLY — it is graded nowhere and it never changes the action. Read it as 'where the desk collectively sits versus the number'.

coherence.note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

paragraphs: This one lives on the bullpens, the shape of the matchup, and our four analysts. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a home pen with nobody working back-to-back, the home starter is known and the home starter's walk rate is below 0.09, and both starters are known and the two starters' average strikeout rate is below 0.23. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: This is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst's P(over) is below 0.53, both starters are known and the two starters' gap in contact allowed (home minus away) is at least -0.03, and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is below 1. That side of it is the straightforward one.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Aug 4 to Aug 20) it played 180 of the 226 games it saw, and it went 120-51-9.

desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.

definition.max_score_why: the measure is strictly below 1 at any finite amount of evidence, so no pick is ever shown as 100
definition.formula: p = (for + 1) / (for + against + 2); confidence = min(99, round(100 * max(0, 2p - 1)))
definition.prior: uniform (Beta(1,1)) — the standard uninformative choice, pre-specified, not fitted to any board
definition.why_not: pick_strength divides by every seated strategy, abstentions included. On a 31-seat committee where the top pick draws about 4 seats that puts every pick under the 0.25 cut, so every pick reads 'lean' and the measure separates nothing. This measure divides by the seats that actually voted and uses the +1/+2 smoothing to keep a thin unanimous room below a deep one — which is the objection pick_strength raises against dividing by votes cast.

paragraphs: This one lives on the bullpens, the shape of the matchup, and our four analysts. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a home pen with nobody working back-to-back, the home starter is known and the home starter's walk rate is below 0.09, and both starters are known and the two starters' average strikeout rate is below 0.23. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: This is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst's P(over) is below 0.53, both starters are known and the two starters' gap in contact allowed (home minus away) is at least -0.03, and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is below 1. That side of it is the straightforward one.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Aug 4 to Aug 20) it played 180 of the 226 games it saw, and it went 120-51-9.

paragraphs: Riding a 5-game winning run, the Royals take on the Tigers at Kauffman Stadium on Friday. Troy Melton (7-1, 1.49 ERA) starts for the Tigers. Melton went 4 1/3 innings last time out, giving up 3 runs on 8 hits with 1 walk and 4 strikeouts in a 4-3 loss against the White Sox on Saturday. Noah Cameron (7-8, 4.16 ERA) opposes him for the Royals, and he threw 9 shutout innings last time out, giving up 1 hit and 1 walk with 8 strikeouts in a 3-0 win at Los Angeles on Sunday.
We come down on the under of this number. The total opened at 8 and has not moved off it. The ballpark here has played right at league-average scoring over the last three years.
The rest of it agrees: the Tigers went to 0 relievers yesterday and Melton takes the ball on 6 days' rest.

The Royals are 55-74 and have won 5 in a row; the Tigers are 61-66 and have lost 2 in a row. The Royals have scored 4.6 runs a game over their last fifteen, the Tigers 4.8. The season series is 6-4 to the Tigers.

pregame_line.note: THE PREGAME LINE, LOCKED: The market state at the LAST wall before first pitch — the number this game actually started at, captured from the point-in-time serve fact store (every captured row's decision timestamp is provably before first pitch). It is refreshed only while the game has not started; the first cycle after first pitch stamps locked_at and the record is immutable forever after. Every analyst read on the card carries `vs_line` — the exact line THAT engine was priced against — so a card can say 'the conditions analyst: OVER 8.5 (priced vs 8.5)' and you can see at a glance whether an analyst is on the same number as the locked pregame line.

analysts.name: VEGA · The Price
analysts.persona_line: The number is the evidence, so I grade the market and nothing else: where it opened, how far it moved, how much the books disagree and what the two sides actually cost.
analysts.completeness_note: The price analyst read its whole slice on this game at T-3h: 8 of 8 levers populated, 100% of its model's weight.
analysts.take: The board de-vigs to 51.1% over on 8 and I read 54.2% — I'm taking the over. I bet the disagreement, not the level.

analysts.name: ATLAS · The Conditions
analysts.persona_line: Runs are a physical event, so I grade the place and the man behind the plate: the park's run factor, its altitude and roof, day or night, and how many runs this umpire's games actually produce.
analysts.completeness_note: The conditions analyst read its whole slice on this game at T-3h: 7 of 7 levers populated, 100% of its model's weight.
analysts.take: I grade the place and the umpire and nothing else. On those alone: over 8, 51%.
analysts.live_state_note: Top 2nd — this state sits outside my certified range, so no number. Watching.

analysts.name: NOVA · The Bats
analysts.persona_line: Runs come from bats, so I grade the hitters and nothing else: the nine names actually posted tonight against the hand they will face, and how the two offenses have actually been scoring.
analysts.completeness_note: The hitting analyst filed this read at T-3h without the nine names actually posted — those levers took their neutral value and contributed nothing to the call. 6 of 9 levers populated, carrying 92% of the model's weight, so the read stands on what it genuinely knows and its conviction is reduced to match.
analysts.take: I grade hitters and nothing else — not the arms, not the park, not the price. The bats say over 8 at 50%.

analysts.name: SCOUT · The Arms
analysts.persona_line: Runs come from bad pitching, so I grade the arms and nothing else: the two starters who open the game and the bullpens behind them — weak staffs mean runs, and I lean over.
analysts.completeness_note: The pitching analyst read its whole slice on this game at T-3h: 14 of 14 levers populated, 100% of its model's weight.
analysts.take: Everything starts with who's throwing. 0.11 runs off neutral on the arms, under 8 — I'll take that against the room.

spread.note: THE ANALYST CONSENSUS IS TOTALS-ONLY. Every v2 read is scope=full_game, bet_type=total — not one of the four produces a run-line call, so every voice here is null and the state is PENDING, permanently and by design. This dimension used to attribute a margin side to the conditions analyst (from the simulator's joint margin distribution) and to the hitting analyst (from the run-line lean stream). Those were the DISMANTLED engines that used to carry those names; the v2 the conditions analyst reads the conditions and the v2 the hitting analyst reads the bats, and neither has anything to say about a margin. The key is kept at null rather than removed so nothing downstream changes shape. THE RUN-LINE CALL ITSELF DID NOT GO ANYWHERE: It is served at games[].diamondedge.spread_call, attributed to its actual producers.

diamondedge.rationale_line: We're on the under 8.5 at -105 (3★) — that is where the price edge is. The desk disagrees: three of the four analysts with a read lean over. That disagreement is context, not a veto — no consensus configuration has separated from chance, so it does not move the bet.

ou_call.note: side IS the served bet whenever one was served (side_basis=served_bet); it falls back to the desk's own majority lean only when nothing was served, and a lean is never a bet.

spread_call.rationale_line: Both margin producers like the home side of the run line — the run-line stream's direction and the simulated margin agree.
spread_call.note: displayed prediction synthesized from the two MARGIN PRODUCERS — the run-line lean stream and the simulator's joint margin. Neither is one of the four analysts: the v2 stream is totals-only and no analyst produces a run-line call, so these voices are named for what they are. The run-line lean stream keeps grading unchanged in its own ledger, and the margin engine's betting-certification status is irrelevant for display.

predicted_score.note: per-team MEDIAN runs from the simulator's joint distribution (ties broken toward the winner per P(home win)). Display prediction only — graded nowhere.

why: walk-forward, the fitted weights are not distinguishable from equal weighting (delta log-loss -0.00032, 95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025] on 434 games over 34 days)
desk_fit.gate: adopt fitted weights only when the trailing window holds >= 300 graded games with >= 100 reads for every analyst AND the walk-forward log-loss improvement over equal weighting has a 95% day-clustered interval strictly better than zero

source.note: the v2 stream's own append-only GRADED LEDGER — the graded half of the write-once board that analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date() serves the desk chief, so the combiner and the chief describe the same desk. Read only; nothing here re-prices or re-grades. Pushes carry no outcome and are dropped, as are games whose analysts were priced at different lines and landed between them.
source.no_longer_read: v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — the walk-forward reconstruction of the PREVIOUS four analysts (the price analyst the champion engine, the hitting analyst the v4 grid, the conditions analyst the simulator, the pitching analyst the simple-8 fundamentals). Those four were dismantled on 2026-07-31; a weight fitted on their behaviour is not a weight for the analysts it would be applied to. The file is left on disk untouched — nothing is deleted or restated — and is simply never opened by this module.
source.fence: no frame on or before 2026-06-30 — the four models were fitted through that date, so a frame at or before it would be a fit on training data

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 434 games and 34 days the log-loss difference is -0.00032 (95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

The four sides sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points, printed beside each rate. What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. What each side earns from here is the forward record's to say, nightly and in public.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT, HELD TO A HARD BAR. Every night it re-fits, over the trailing 30 days, how each analyst's disagreement with the price has related to results — scored strictly WALK-FORWARD, fitted only on days before the day it is scored on — and holds the fit to two baselines at once: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are adopted only when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting is strictly clear of zero and the window carries enough reads to fit four weights; until they earn that, the desk weights its analysts equally and prints the numbers. The +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet.

desk_combined.note: the desk's weighted combination of the four analysts' disagreement with the price. DISPLAY ONLY — it is graded nowhere and it never changes the action. Read it as 'where the desk collectively sits versus the number'.

coherence.note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

chief.action_basis: served bet + star tier (AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served)

pattern.line: When the desk splits 3-1, the side they called has landed 51% of the time (n=154, live; 95% CI 43%-59%, even with the market).

chief.rationale_line: We're on the under 8.5 at -105 (3★) — that is where the price edge is. The desk disagrees: three of the four analysts with a read lean over. That disagreement is context, not a veto — no consensus configuration has separated from chance, so it does not move the bet.
chief.note: THE CHIEF (Leon, 2026-07-30; SEMANTICS REWRITTEN 2026-07-31): DiamondEdge's own PREGAME synthesis — the O/U call, the run-line call and the predicted final score, all against the LOCKED pregame line, with a rationale grounded in the MEASURED tables. THE COHERENCE RULE (the 2026-07-31 fix): when the engine SERVED A BET, the chief's O/U call IS that bet — same side, same number — and the action can never be AVOID. AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served. The desk's disagreement with a served bet is real and is stated (desk_agreement + the rationale line), but it is stated as CONTEXT, never as 'we're passing' on a bet we are actually making. The chief remains PRESENTATION and ROUTING ONLY: the measured pattern table can change the language and move a displayed action DOWN one rung, never up, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and on a served bet the ladder bottoms out at LEAN. Betting stays with the +EV gate and the star system, exactly as before. predicted_score and desk_combined are display predictions, graded nowhere.

pick.star_tier: Rule pick — the day's rule called this side

confidence.what_it_is: One rule chose every pick on this board and makes no distinction between them, so there is no per-game vote to read. This is the rule's own win-loss record over its lookback window, on the same 0-100 scale — the same number for every pick on the board.
confidence.counts_all_picks: Every pick counts in the record at every confidence score. This is a CUT of the served population, never a filter on it.

definition.max_score_why: the measure is strictly below 1 at any finite amount of evidence, so no pick is ever shown as 100
definition.formula: p = (for + 1) / (for + against + 2); confidence = min(99, round(100 * max(0, 2p - 1)))
definition.prior: uniform (Beta(1,1)) — the standard uninformative choice, pre-specified, not fitted to any board
definition.why_not: pick_strength divides by every seated strategy, abstentions included. On a 31-seat committee where the top pick draws about 4 seats that puts every pick under the 0.25 cut, so every pick reads 'lean' and the measure separates nothing. This measure divides by the seats that actually voted and uses the +1/+2 smoothing to keep a thin unanimous room below a deep one — which is the objection pick_strength raises against dividing by votes cast.
definition.counts_all_picks: Every pick counts in the record at every confidence score. This is a CUT of the served population, never a filter on it.

confidence.rule: Bet OVER when the home arms working back-to-back is below 1 and the home starter is known and the home starter's walk rate is below 0.09 and both starters are known and the two starters' average strikeout rate is below 0.23. Otherwise bet UNDER when the conditions analyst's P(over) is below 0.53 and both starters are known and the two starters' gap in contact allowed (home minus away) is at least -0.03 and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is below 1. Otherwise pass.
confidence.pushes_excluded: a push decided nothing, so it is not counted for or against; it is reported here so the record still adds up

forge_strategy.search_scope: Every rule the search can write was applied, unchanged, to every game on every night of the window, and scored on one thing: how many more times it won than it lost. Nothing else was ranked on.
forge_strategy.summary_line: Today's board is one rule. It came out of last night's search with the best win-minus-loss record over the window, and it was frozen before the first game. Over the 17 nights it was chosen on (2026-08-04 to 2026-08-20), this rule went 120-51-9.
forge_strategy.selected_reason: Every rule the search can write was applied, unchanged, to every game on every night of the lookback window. The rule that finished with the best record of wins minus losses was frozen and applied to today's slate. The window ends before today, so no game on this board was part of choosing the rule.
forge_strategy.line_basis: The pick is served at the locked pregame line and its real price. A game with no line, or no price at that line, is not served at all.

forge_strategy.tier_basis: One rule chose every pick on this board and it makes no distinction between them, so every forge pick carries the same display tier. There is no per-pick conviction to report.
forge_strategy.progressive_note: The rule is frozen before the day starts. Each game gets its call the moment its inputs land, against that same frozen rule — never a re-search, and never a different rule later in the day.

Every analyst read on the card carries `vs_line` — the exact line THAT engine was priced against — so a card can say 'the conditions analyst: OVER 8.5 (priced vs 8.5)' and you can see at a glance whether an analyst is on the same number as the locked pregame line.

spread.note: THE ANALYST CONSENSUS IS TOTALS-ONLY. Every v2 read is scope=full_game, bet_type=total — not one of the four produces a run-line call, so every voice here is null and the state is PENDING, permanently and by design. This dimension used to attribute a margin side to the conditions analyst (from the simulator's joint margin distribution) and to the hitting analyst (from the run-line lean stream). Those were the DISMANTLED engines that used to carry those names; the v2 the conditions analyst reads the conditions and the v2 the hitting analyst reads the bats, and neither has anything to say about a margin. The key is kept at null rather than removed so nothing downstream changes shape. THE RUN-LINE CALL ITSELF DID NOT GO ANYWHERE: It is served at games[].diamondedge.spread_call, attributed to its actual producers.

diamondedge.rationale_line: We're on the under 8.5 at -115 (3★) — that is where the price edge is. The desk disagrees: three of the four analysts with a read lean over. That disagreement is context, not a veto — no consensus configuration has separated from chance, so it does not move the bet.

Neither is one of the four analysts: the v2 stream is totals-only and no analyst produces a run-line call, so these voices are named for what they are. The run-line lean stream keeps grading unchanged in its own ledger, and the margin engine's betting-certification status is irrelevant for display.
