desk_fit.gate: adopt fitted weights only when the trailing window holds >= 300 graded games with >= 100 reads for every analyst AND the walk-forward log-loss improvement over equal weighting has a 95% day-clustered interval strictly better than zero

source.note: the v2 stream's own append-only GRADED LEDGER — the graded half of the write-once board that analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date() serves the desk chief, so the combiner and the chief describe the same desk. Read only; nothing here re-prices or re-grades. Pushes carry no outcome and are dropped, as are games whose analysts were priced at different lines and landed between them.
source.no_longer_read: v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — the walk-forward reconstruction of the PREVIOUS four analysts (the price analyst the champion engine, the hitting analyst the v4 grid, the conditions analyst the simulator, the pitching analyst the simple-8 fundamentals). Those four were dismantled on 2026-07-31; a weight fitted on their behaviour is not a weight for the analysts it would be applied to. The file is left on disk untouched — nothing is deleted or restated — and is simply never opened by this module.
source.fence: no frame on or before 2026-06-30 — the four models were fitted through that date, so a frame at or before it would be a fit on training data

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 434 games and 34 days the log-loss difference is -0.00032 (95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

The four sides sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points, printed beside each rate. What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. What each side earns from here is the forward record's to say, nightly and in public.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT, HELD TO A HARD BAR. Every night it re-fits, over the trailing 30 days, how each analyst's disagreement with the price has related to results — scored strictly WALK-FORWARD, fitted only on days before the day it is scored on — and holds the fit to two baselines at once: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are adopted only when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting is strictly clear of zero and the window carries enough reads to fit four weights; until they earn that, the desk weights its analysts equally and prints the numbers. The +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet.

desk_combined.note: the desk's weighted combination of the four analysts' disagreement with the price. DISPLAY ONLY — it is graded nowhere and it never changes the action. Read it as 'where the desk collectively sits versus the number'.

coherence.note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

chief.note: THE CHIEF (Leon, 2026-07-30; SEMANTICS REWRITTEN 2026-07-31): DiamondEdge's own PREGAME synthesis — the O/U call, the run-line call and the predicted final score, all against the LOCKED pregame line, with a rationale grounded in the MEASURED tables. THE COHERENCE RULE (the 2026-07-31 fix): when the engine SERVED A BET, the chief's O/U call IS that bet — same side, same number — and the action can never be AVOID. AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served. The desk's disagreement with a served bet is real and is stated (desk_agreement + the rationale line), but it is stated as CONTEXT, never as 'we're passing' on a bet we are actually making. The chief remains PRESENTATION and ROUTING ONLY: the measured pattern table can change the language and move a displayed action DOWN one rung, never up, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and on a served bet the ladder bottoms out at LEAN. Betting stays with the +EV gate and the star system, exactly as before. predicted_score and desk_combined are display predictions, graded nowhere.

confidence.what_it_is: One rule chose every pick on this board and makes no distinction between them, so there is no per-game vote to read. This is the rule's own win-loss record over its lookback window, on the same 0-100 scale — the same number for every pick on the board.
confidence.counts_all_picks: Every pick counts in the record at every confidence score. This is a CUT of the served population, never a filter on it.

definition.max_score_why: the measure is strictly below 1 at any finite amount of evidence, so no pick is ever shown as 100
definition.formula: p = (for + 1) / (for + against + 2); confidence = min(99, round(100 * max(0, 2p - 1)))
definition.prior: uniform (Beta(1,1)) — the standard uninformative choice, pre-specified, not fitted to any board
definition.why_not: pick_strength divides by every seated strategy, abstentions included. On a 31-seat committee where the top pick draws about 4 seats that puts every pick under the 0.25 cut, so every pick reads 'lean' and the measure separates nothing. This measure divides by the seats that actually voted and uses the +1/+2 smoothing to keep a thin unanimous room below a deep one — which is the objection pick_strength raises against dividing by votes cast.
definition.counts_all_picks: Every pick counts in the record at every confidence score. This is a CUT of the served population, never a filter on it.

paragraphs: This one lives on the bullpens, the shape of the matchup, and our four analysts. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a home pen with nobody working back-to-back, the home starter is known and the home starter's walk rate is below 0.09, and both starters are known and the two starters' average strikeout rate is below 0.23. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: This is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst's P(over) is below 0.53, both starters are known and the two starters' gap in contact allowed (home minus away) is at least -0.03, and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is below 1. That side of it is the straightforward one.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Aug 4 to Aug 20) it played 180 of the 226 games it saw, and it went 120-51-9.

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 434 games and 34 days the log-loss difference is -0.00032 (95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

The four sides sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points, printed beside each rate. What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. What each side earns from here is the forward record's to say, nightly and in public.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT, HELD TO A HARD BAR. Every night it re-fits, over the trailing 30 days, how each analyst's disagreement with the price has related to results — scored strictly WALK-FORWARD, fitted only on days before the day it is scored on — and holds the fit to two baselines at once: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are adopted only when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting is strictly clear of zero and the window carries enough reads to fit four weights; until they earn that, the desk weights its analysts equally and prints the numbers. The +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet.

The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

paragraphs: This one lives on the bullpens, the shape of the matchup, and our four analysts. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a home pen with nobody working back-to-back, the home starter is known and the home starter's walk rate is below 0.09, and both starters are known and the two starters' average strikeout rate is below 0.23. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: This is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst's P(over) is below 0.53, both starters are known and the two starters' gap in contact allowed (home minus away) is at least -0.03, and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is below 1. That side of it is the straightforward one.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Aug 4 to Aug 20) it played 180 of the 226 games it saw, and it went 120-51-9.

definition.max_score_why: the measure is strictly below 1 at any finite amount of evidence, so no pick is ever shown as 100
definition.formula: p = (for + 1) / (for + against + 2); confidence = min(99, round(100 * max(0, 2p - 1)))
definition.prior: uniform (Beta(1,1)) — the standard uninformative choice, pre-specified, not fitted to any board
definition.why_not: pick_strength divides by every seated strategy, abstentions included. On a 31-seat committee where the top pick draws about 4 seats that puts every pick under the 0.25 cut, so every pick reads 'lean' and the measure separates nothing. This measure divides by the seats that actually voted and uses the +1/+2 smoothing to keep a thin unanimous room below a deep one — which is the objection pick_strength raises against dividing by votes cast.

paragraphs: This one lives on the bullpens, the shape of the matchup, and our four analysts. It is a 6-condition read, and it wants every one of them before it says anything at all.

It takes the OVER when it finds a home pen with nobody working back-to-back, the home starter is known and the home starter's walk rate is below 0.09, and both starters are known and the two starters' average strikeout rate is below 0.23. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: This is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst's P(over) is below 0.53, both starters are known and the two starters' gap in contact allowed (home minus away) is at least -0.03, and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is below 1. That side of it is the straightforward one.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Aug 4 to Aug 20) it played 180 of the 226 games it saw, and it went 120-51-9.

pregame_line.note: THE PREGAME LINE, LOCKED: The market state at the LAST wall before first pitch — the number this game actually started at, captured from the point-in-time serve fact store (every captured row's decision timestamp is provably before first pitch). It is refreshed only while the game has not started; the first cycle after first pitch stamps locked_at and the record is immutable forever after. Every analyst read on the card carries `vs_line` — the exact line THAT engine was priced against — so a card can say 'the conditions analyst: OVER 8.5 (priced vs 8.5)' and you can see at a glance whether an analyst is on the same number as the locked pregame line.

line_now.note: the CURRENT read of the SAME full-game pregame totals market the locked line was captured from, display only. It exists so a pregame move never mutates the locked line. It is suppressed entirely once the game starts — after first pitch there is no pregame market to compare against. The comparison is same-book, or else both sides use the identical book-consensus-median basis (books are never mixed), and a comparison implying an implausible full-game move is refused rather than shipped. In-play/remaining-runs totals are never read here. Never graded, never a bet, never in any record.

analysts.name: VEGA · The Price
analysts.persona_line: The number is the evidence, so I grade the market and nothing else: where it opened, how far it moved, how much the books disagree and what the two sides actually cost.
analysts.completeness_note: The price analyst read its whole slice on this game at T-3h: 8 of 8 levers populated, 100% of its model's weight.
analysts.take: The board de-vigs to 48.1% over on 8.5 and I read 49.0% — I'm taking the over. I bet the disagreement, not the level.

analysts.name: ATLAS · The Conditions
analysts.persona_line: Runs are a physical event, so I grade the place and the man behind the plate: the park's run factor, its altitude and roof, day or night, and how many runs this umpire's games actually produce.
analysts.completeness_note: The conditions analyst read its whole slice on this game at T-3h: 7 of 7 levers populated, 100% of its model's weight.
analysts.take: The conditions are loud here — 0.26 runs of deviation from a neutral night, and they point over on 8.5.

analysts.name: NOVA · The Bats
analysts.persona_line: Runs come from bats, so I grade the hitters and nothing else: the nine names actually posted tonight against the hand they will face, and how the two offenses have actually been scoring.
analysts.completeness_note: The hitting analyst filed this read at T-3h without the nine names actually posted — those levers took their neutral value and contributed nothing to the call. 6 of 9 levers populated, carrying 92% of the model's weight, so the read stands on what it genuinely knows and its conviction is reduced to match.
analysts.take: Somebody has to actually score the runs. The bats are 0.43 off neutral and they say under at 8.5 — the rest of the desk can argue.

analysts.name: SCOUT · The Arms
analysts.persona_line: Runs come from bad pitching, so I grade the arms and nothing else: the two starters who open the game and the bullpens behind them — weak staffs mean runs, and I lean over.
analysts.completeness_note: The pitching analyst read its whole slice on this game at T-3h: 14 of 14 levers populated, 100% of its model's weight.
analysts.take: Two starters and the two bullpens behind them, and nothing else: 0.08 runs above an average staff — 8.6 against 8.5.

spread.note: THE ANALYST CONSENSUS IS TOTALS-ONLY. Every v2 read is scope=full_game, bet_type=total — not one of the four produces a run-line call, so every voice here is null and the state is PENDING, permanently and by design. This dimension used to attribute a margin side to the conditions analyst (from the simulator's joint margin distribution) and to the hitting analyst (from the run-line lean stream). Those were the DISMANTLED engines that used to carry those names; the v2 the conditions analyst reads the conditions and the v2 the hitting analyst reads the bats, and neither has anything to say about a margin. The key is kept at null rather than removed so nothing downstream changes shape. THE RUN-LINE CALL ITSELF DID NOT GO ANYWHERE: It is served at games[].diamondedge.spread_call, attributed to its actual producers.

diamondedge.rationale_line: We're on the under 8.5 at -110 (3★) — that is where the price edge is. The desk disagrees: three of the four analysts with a read lean over. That disagreement is context, not a veto — no consensus configuration has separated from chance, so it does not move the bet.

ou_call.note: side IS the served bet whenever one was served (side_basis=served_bet); it falls back to the desk's own majority lean only when nothing was served, and a lean is never a bet.

spread_call.rationale_line: Both margin producers like the away side of the run line — the run-line stream's direction and the simulated margin agree.
spread_call.note: displayed prediction synthesized from the two MARGIN PRODUCERS — the run-line lean stream and the simulator's joint margin. Neither is one of the four analysts: the v2 stream is totals-only and no analyst produces a run-line call, so these voices are named for what they are. The run-line lean stream keeps grading unchanged in its own ledger, and the margin engine's betting-certification status is irrelevant for display.

predicted_score.note: per-team MEDIAN runs from the simulator's joint distribution (ties broken toward the winner per P(home win)). Display prediction only — graded nowhere.

why: walk-forward, the fitted weights are not distinguishable from equal weighting (delta log-loss -0.00032, 95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025] on 434 games over 34 days)
desk_fit.gate: adopt fitted weights only when the trailing window holds >= 300 graded games with >= 100 reads for every analyst AND the walk-forward log-loss improvement over equal weighting has a 95% day-clustered interval strictly better than zero

source.note: the v2 stream's own append-only GRADED LEDGER — the graded half of the write-once board that analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date() serves the desk chief, so the combiner and the chief describe the same desk. Read only; nothing here re-prices or re-grades. Pushes carry no outcome and are dropped, as are games whose analysts were priced at different lines and landed between them.
source.no_longer_read: v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — the walk-forward reconstruction of the PREVIOUS four analysts (the price analyst the champion engine, the hitting analyst the v4 grid, the conditions analyst the simulator, the pitching analyst the simple-8 fundamentals). Those four were dismantled on 2026-07-31; a weight fitted on their behaviour is not a weight for the analysts it would be applied to. The file is left on disk untouched — nothing is deleted or restated — and is simply never opened by this module.
source.fence: no frame on or before 2026-06-30 — the four models were fitted through that date, so a frame at or before it would be a fit on training data

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 434 games and 34 days the log-loss difference is -0.00032 (95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

The four sides sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points, printed beside each rate. What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. What each side earns from here is the forward record's to say, nightly and in public.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT, HELD TO A HARD BAR. Every night it re-fits, over the trailing 30 days, how each analyst's disagreement with the price has related to results — scored strictly WALK-FORWARD, fitted only on days before the day it is scored on — and holds the fit to two baselines at once: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are adopted only when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting is strictly clear of zero and the window carries enough reads to fit four weights; until they earn that, the desk weights its analysts equally and prints the numbers. The +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet.

desk_combined.note: the desk's weighted combination of the four analysts' disagreement with the price. DISPLAY ONLY — it is graded nowhere and it never changes the action. Read it as 'where the desk collectively sits versus the number'.

coherence.note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

chief.action_basis: served bet + star tier (AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served)

pattern.line: When the desk splits 3-1, the side they called has landed 51% of the time (n=154, live; 95% CI 43%-59%, even with the market).

chief.rationale_line: We're on the under 8.5 at -110 (3★) — that is where the price edge is. The desk disagrees: three of the four analysts with a read lean over. That disagreement is context, not a veto — no consensus configuration has separated from chance, so it does not move the bet.
chief.note: THE CHIEF (Leon, 2026-07-30; SEMANTICS REWRITTEN 2026-07-31): DiamondEdge's own PREGAME synthesis — the O/U call, the run-line call and the predicted final score, all against the LOCKED pregame line, with a rationale grounded in the MEASURED tables. THE COHERENCE RULE (the 2026-07-31 fix): when the engine SERVED A BET, the chief's O/U call IS that bet — same side, same number — and the action can never be AVOID. AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served. The desk's disagreement with a served bet is real and is stated (desk_agreement + the rationale line), but it is stated as CONTEXT, never as 'we're passing' on a bet we are actually making. The chief remains PRESENTATION and ROUTING ONLY: the measured pattern table can change the language and move a displayed action DOWN one rung, never up, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and on a served bet the ladder bottoms out at LEAN. Betting stays with the +EV gate and the star system, exactly as before. predicted_score and desk_combined are display predictions, graded nowhere.

pick.star_tier: Rule pick — the day's rule called this side

confidence.what_it_is: One rule chose every pick on this board and makes no distinction between them, so there is no per-game vote to read. This is the rule's own win-loss record over its lookback window, on the same 0-100 scale — the same number for every pick on the board.
confidence.counts_all_picks: Every pick counts in the record at every confidence score. This is a CUT of the served population, never a filter on it.

definition.max_score_why: the measure is strictly below 1 at any finite amount of evidence, so no pick is ever shown as 100
definition.formula: p = (for + 1) / (for + against + 2); confidence = min(99, round(100 * max(0, 2p - 1)))
definition.prior: uniform (Beta(1,1)) — the standard uninformative choice, pre-specified, not fitted to any board
definition.why_not: pick_strength divides by every seated strategy, abstentions included. On a 31-seat committee where the top pick draws about 4 seats that puts every pick under the 0.25 cut, so every pick reads 'lean' and the measure separates nothing. This measure divides by the seats that actually voted and uses the +1/+2 smoothing to keep a thin unanimous room below a deep one — which is the objection pick_strength raises against dividing by votes cast.
definition.counts_all_picks: Every pick counts in the record at every confidence score. This is a CUT of the served population, never a filter on it.

Otherwise pass.
confidence.pushes_excluded: a push decided nothing, so it is not counted for or against; it is reported here so the record still adds up

It takes the OVER when it finds a home pen with nobody working back-to-back, the home starter is known and the home starter's walk rate is below 0.09, and both starters are known and the two starters' average strikeout rate is below 0.23. None of that is the textbook case for the over — it is much closer to the case for the under. That is the point of it: This is a spot where the obvious read has been the wrong one. When the picture turns over, so does it — the UNDER when it finds the conditions analyst's P(over) is below 0.53, both starters are known and the two starters' gap in contact allowed (home minus away) is at least -0.03, and the desk's edge measured against how much the desk disagrees with itself is below 1. That side of it is the straightforward one.

Anything that does not fit one of those shapes it leaves alone. A pass is the rule working, not the rule missing. Over the 17 nights that chose it (Aug 4 to Aug 20) it played 180 of the 226 games it saw, and it went 120-51-9.

pregame_line.note: THE PREGAME LINE, LOCKED: The market state at the LAST wall before first pitch — the number this game actually started at, captured from the point-in-time serve fact store (every captured row's decision timestamp is provably before first pitch). It is refreshed only while the game has not started; the first cycle after first pitch stamps locked_at and the record is immutable forever after. Every analyst read on the card carries `vs_line` — the exact line THAT engine was priced against — so a card can say 'the conditions analyst: OVER 8.5 (priced vs 8.5)' and you can see at a glance whether an analyst is on the same number as the locked pregame line.

line_now.note: the CURRENT read of the SAME full-game pregame totals market the locked line was captured from, display only. It exists so a pregame move never mutates the locked line. It is suppressed entirely once the game starts — after first pitch there is no pregame market to compare against. The comparison is same-book, or else both sides use the identical book-consensus-median basis (books are never mixed), and a comparison implying an implausible full-game move is refused rather than shipped. In-play/remaining-runs totals are never read here. Never graded, never a bet, never in any record.

spread.note: THE ANALYST CONSENSUS IS TOTALS-ONLY. Every v2 read is scope=full_game, bet_type=total — not one of the four produces a run-line call, so every voice here is null and the state is PENDING, permanently and by design. This dimension used to attribute a margin side to the conditions analyst (from the simulator's joint margin distribution) and to the hitting analyst (from the run-line lean stream). Those were the DISMANTLED engines that used to carry those names; the v2 the conditions analyst reads the conditions and the v2 the hitting analyst reads the bats, and neither has anything to say about a margin. The key is kept at null rather than removed so nothing downstream changes shape. THE RUN-LINE CALL ITSELF DID NOT GO ANYWHERE: It is served at games[].diamondedge.spread_call, attributed to its actual producers.

diamondedge.rationale_line: We're on the over 8.0 at +100 (3★) — that is where the price edge is. The desk disagrees: three of the four analysts with a read lean under. That disagreement is context, not a veto — no consensus configuration has separated from chance, so it does not move the bet.

ou_call.note: side IS the served bet whenever one was served (side_basis=served_bet); it falls back to the desk's own majority lean only when nothing was served, and a lean is never a bet.

spread_call.rationale_line: The run-line stream leans away; the margin simulator has no read on this game yet.
spread_call.note: displayed prediction synthesized from the two MARGIN PRODUCERS — the run-line lean stream and the simulator's joint margin. Neither is one of the four analysts: the v2 stream is totals-only and no analyst produces a run-line call, so these voices are named for what they are. The run-line lean stream keeps grading unchanged in its own ledger, and the margin engine's betting-certification status is irrelevant for display.

predicted_score.note: per-team MEDIAN runs from the simulator's joint distribution (ties broken toward the winner per P(home win)). Display prediction only — graded nowhere.

why: walk-forward, the fitted weights are not distinguishable from equal weighting (delta log-loss -0.00032, 95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025] on 434 games over 34 days)
desk_fit.gate: adopt fitted weights only when the trailing window holds >= 300 graded games with >= 100 reads for every analyst AND the walk-forward log-loss improvement over equal weighting has a 95% day-clustered interval strictly better than zero

source.note: the v2 stream's own append-only GRADED LEDGER — the graded half of the write-once board that analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date() serves the desk chief, so the combiner and the chief describe the same desk. Read only; nothing here re-prices or re-grades. Pushes carry no outcome and are dropped, as are games whose analysts were priced at different lines and landed between them.
source.no_longer_read: v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — the walk-forward reconstruction of the PREVIOUS four analysts (the price analyst the champion engine, the hitting analyst the v4 grid, the conditions analyst the simulator, the pitching analyst the simple-8 fundamentals). Those four were dismantled on 2026-07-31; a weight fitted on their behaviour is not a weight for the analysts it would be applied to. The file is left on disk untouched — nothing is deleted or restated — and is simply never opened by this module.
source.fence: no frame on or before 2026-06-30 — the four models were fitted through that date, so a frame at or before it would be a fit on training data

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 434 games and 34 days the log-loss difference is -0.00032 (95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

The four sides sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points, printed beside each rate. What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. What each side earns from here is the forward record's to say, nightly and in public.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT, HELD TO A HARD BAR. Every night it re-fits, over the trailing 30 days, how each analyst's disagreement with the price has related to results — scored strictly WALK-FORWARD, fitted only on days before the day it is scored on — and holds the fit to two baselines at once: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are adopted only when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting is strictly clear of zero and the window carries enough reads to fit four weights; until they earn that, the desk weights its analysts equally and prints the numbers. The +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet.

desk_combined.note: the desk's weighted combination of the four analysts' disagreement with the price. DISPLAY ONLY — it is graded nowhere and it never changes the action. Read it as 'where the desk collectively sits versus the number'.

coherence.note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

chief.action_basis: served bet + star tier (AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served)

pattern.line: When the desk splits 3-1, the side they called has landed 51% of the time (n=154, live; 95% CI 43%-59%, even with the market).

chief.rationale_line: We're on the over 8.0 at +100 (3★) — that is where the price edge is. The desk disagrees: three of the four analysts with a read lean under. That disagreement is context, not a veto — no consensus configuration has separated from chance, so it does not move the bet.
chief.note: THE CHIEF (Leon, 2026-07-30; SEMANTICS REWRITTEN 2026-07-31): DiamondEdge's own PREGAME synthesis — the O/U call, the run-line call and the predicted final score, all against the LOCKED pregame line, with a rationale grounded in the MEASURED tables. THE COHERENCE RULE (the 2026-07-31 fix): when the engine SERVED A BET, the chief's O/U call IS that bet — same side, same number — and the action can never be AVOID. AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served. The desk's disagreement with a served bet is real and is stated (desk_agreement + the rationale line), but it is stated as CONTEXT, never as 'we're passing' on a bet we are actually making. The chief remains PRESENTATION and ROUTING ONLY: the measured pattern table can change the language and move a displayed action DOWN one rung, never up, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and on a served bet the ladder bottoms out at LEAN. Betting stays with the +EV gate and the star system, exactly as before. predicted_score and desk_combined are display predictions, graded nowhere.

analysts.persona_line: Runs are a physical event, so I grade the place and the man behind the plate: the park's run factor, its altitude and roof, day or night, and how many runs this umpire's games actually produce.
analysts.completeness_note: The conditions analyst filed this read at T-3h without the ballpark and the time of day — those levers took their neutral value and contributed nothing to the call. 4 of 7 levers populated, carrying 15% of the model's weight, so the read stands on what it genuinely knows and its conviction is reduced to match.
analysts.take: On the conditions I read, it is over 8 at 51%.

analysts.name: NOVA · The Bats
analysts.persona_line: Runs come from bats, so I grade the hitters and nothing else: the nine names actually posted tonight against the hand they will face, and how the two offenses have actually been scoring.
analysts.completeness_note: The hitting analyst filed this read at T-3h without the nine names actually posted — those levers took their neutral value and contributed nothing to the call. 6 of 9 levers populated, carrying 92% of the model's weight, so the read stands on what it genuinely knows and its conviction is reduced to match.
analysts.take: On the bats, it is over 8 at 54%.

analysts.name: SCOUT · The Arms
analysts.persona_line: Runs come from bad pitching, so I grade the arms and nothing else: the two starters who open the game and the bullpens behind them — weak staffs mean runs, and I lean over.
analysts.completeness_note: The pitching analyst read its whole slice on this game at T-3h: 14 of 14 levers populated, 100% of its model's weight.
analysts.take: Everything starts with who's throwing. 0.33 runs off neutral on the arms, under 8 — I'll take that against the room.

spread.note: THE ANALYST CONSENSUS IS TOTALS-ONLY. Every v2 read is scope=full_game, bet_type=total — not one of the four produces a run-line call, so every voice here is null and the state is PENDING, permanently and by design. This dimension used to attribute a margin side to the conditions analyst (from the simulator's joint margin distribution) and to the hitting analyst (from the run-line lean stream). Those were the DISMANTLED engines that used to carry those names; the v2 the conditions analyst reads the conditions and the v2 the hitting analyst reads the bats, and neither has anything to say about a margin. The key is kept at null rather than removed so nothing downstream changes shape. THE RUN-LINE CALL ITSELF DID NOT GO ANYWHERE: It is served at games[].diamondedge.spread_call, attributed to its actual producers.

diamondedge.rationale_line: No bet — most of the desk leans over, but a lean is not a bet and nothing here cleared the price gate.

ou_call.note: side IS the served bet whenever one was served (side_basis=served_bet); it falls back to the desk's own majority lean only when nothing was served, and a lean is never a bet.

spread_call.rationale_line: Both margin producers like the home side of the run line — the run-line stream's direction and the simulated margin agree.
spread_call.note: displayed prediction synthesized from the two MARGIN PRODUCERS — the run-line lean stream and the simulator's joint margin. Neither is one of the four analysts: the v2 stream is totals-only and no analyst produces a run-line call, so these voices are named for what they are. The run-line lean stream keeps grading unchanged in its own ledger, and the margin engine's betting-certification status is irrelevant for display.

predicted_score.note: per-team MEDIAN runs from the simulator's joint distribution (ties broken toward the winner per P(home win)). Display prediction only — graded nowhere.

why: walk-forward, the fitted weights are not distinguishable from equal weighting (delta log-loss -0.00032, 95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025] on 434 games over 34 days)
desk_fit.gate: adopt fitted weights only when the trailing window holds >= 300 graded games with >= 100 reads for every analyst AND the walk-forward log-loss improvement over equal weighting has a 95% day-clustered interval strictly better than zero

source.note: the v2 stream's own append-only GRADED LEDGER — the graded half of the write-once board that analyst_v2_stream.reads_for_date() serves the desk chief, so the combiner and the chief describe the same desk. Read only; nothing here re-prices or re-grades. Pushes carry no outcome and are dropped, as are games whose analysts were priced at different lines and landed between them.
source.no_longer_read: v4/models/analyst_desk/history.parquet — the walk-forward reconstruction of the PREVIOUS four analysts (the price analyst the champion engine, the hitting analyst the v4 grid, the conditions analyst the simulator, the pitching analyst the simple-8 fundamentals). Those four were dismantled on 2026-07-31; a weight fitted on their behaviour is not a weight for the analysts it would be applied to. The file is left on disk untouched — nothing is deleted or restated — and is simply never opened by this module.
source.fence: no frame on or before 2026-06-30 — the four models were fitted through that date, so a frame at or before it would be a fit on training data

desk_fit.headline: Fitting the four analysts' disagreement-with-the-price over a rolling 30-day window does NOT beat weighting them equally: walk-forward over 434 games and 34 days the log-loss difference is -0.00032 (95% CI [-0.00091, +0.00025]). The desk uses EQUAL WEIGHTS. Neither is the combined desk distinguishable from simply using the price.
desk_fit.model: P(over) = sigmoid( logit(p_mkt) + b + SUM_a w_a * d_a ), d_a = logit(p_over_a) - logit(p_mkt_a), 0 where analyst a has no read. The market log-odds are a FIXED OFFSET, so w_a asks only whether that analyst's disagreement with the number adds anything the number does not already carry. Ridge-penalised (lambda pre-specified, not scanned), fit by IRLS, standard errors from the penalised Hessian.
desk_fit.baselines: EQUAL WEIGHT = the same model with one shared coefficient on the mean divergence of the analysts who read the game, fit on the same window — so the comparison isolates differential weighting. MARKET = p_mkt untouched.
caveats: THE CORPUS RESTARTED ON 2026-07-01 AND THAT IS THE POINT. This block used to be computed over ~11,800 games of a pre-re-architecture reconstruction of four DIFFERENT models. Those weights could never have been applied honestly to these analysts, so the history was dropped rather than carried forward. What is here now is a few hundred games and it says so; a thin honest window beats a deep irrelevant one.

Almost every frame is `reconstructed_oos` basis: the four models were built on 2026-07-31 and priced July after the fact. Every read is genuinely out of sample against a 2026-06-30 training fence, but it was not SERVED before the game. The live share grows by one slate a night and nothing is ever restated.

THE EVIDENCE FLOOR IS MET AND THE WALK-FORWARD IS NOT. The trailing window now clears both floors, so four weights CAN be fitted — but the walk-forward that decides whether to USE them only starts once 150 games of history exist, which on a corpus this young costs the first half of it. So the contrast is scored on a handful of slates and its interval is wide enough to contain both a real improvement and a real regression. Adopting weights on it would be adopting noise; the gate stays shut and the interval is printed rather than described.

The four sides sit between 43% and 51% at n=332, an interval of about +/-5.4 points, printed beside each rate. What the re-architecture bought is DECORRELATION — disjoint feature slices, side agreement down from 0.84-0.89 to 0.51-0.57 — which is the property a combiner would need in order to have anything to combine. What each side earns from here is the forward record's to say, nightly and in public.
desk_fit.honest_note: THE ROLLING DESK FIT, HELD TO A HARD BAR. Every night it re-fits, over the trailing 30 days, how each analyst's disagreement with the price has related to results — scored strictly WALK-FORWARD, fitted only on days before the day it is scored on — and holds the fit to two baselines at once: equal weighting and the price itself. Fitted weights are adopted only when the walk-forward improvement over equal weighting is strictly clear of zero and the window carries enough reads to fit four weights; until they earn that, the desk weights its analysts equally and prints the numbers. The +EV gate and the star system remain the only things that make a bet.

desk_combined.note: the desk's weighted combination of the four analysts' disagreement with the price. DISPLAY ONLY — it is graded nowhere and it never changes the action. Read it as 'where the desk collectively sits versus the number'.

coherence.note: THE BET IS `the_bet` and nothing else on this card is a bet. The desk's majority lean, the desk's weighted combination and the conditions analyst's predicted final score are three DISPLAY readings of the same game; each is reported here with whether it points the same way as the ticket. A voice pointing the other way is information, not a contradiction — none of them clears a price gate, and none of them is graded. The run line is a separate market and is never expected to agree with a total.

chief.action_basis: served bet + star tier (AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served)

pattern.line: When the desk splits 3-1, the side they called has landed 51% of the time (n=154, live; 95% CI 43%-59%, even with the market).

chief.rationale_line: No bet — most of the desk leans over, but a lean is not a bet and nothing here cleared the price gate.
chief.note: THE CHIEF (Leon, 2026-07-30; SEMANTICS REWRITTEN 2026-07-31): DiamondEdge's own PREGAME synthesis — the O/U call, the run-line call and the predicted final score, all against the LOCKED pregame line, with a rationale grounded in the MEASURED tables. THE COHERENCE RULE (the 2026-07-31 fix): when the engine SERVED A BET, the chief's O/U call IS that bet — same side, same number — and the action can never be AVOID. AVOID means, and only ever means, that no bet was served. The desk's disagreement with a served bet is real and is stated (desk_agreement + the rationale line), but it is stated as CONTEXT, never as 'we're passing' on a bet we are actually making. The chief remains PRESENTATION and ROUTING ONLY: the measured pattern table can change the language and move a displayed action DOWN one rung, never up, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and on a served bet the ladder bottoms out at LEAN. Betting stays with the +EV gate and the star system, exactly as before. predicted_score and desk_combined are display predictions, graded nowhere.

eras.note: the T-16h era — ended 2026-08-14, it starved the rules of inputs and board volume collapsed 6, 5, 2, 0
T-3h: each game is decided about three hours before its own first pitch, once the analysts have read it and the market has settled
the readiness wall: each game is decided the first hour its inputs are all present and provable — often well before T-3h — and no later than three hours before its own first pitch

picks_post_contract.posted_note: The day's rule is frozen at 3:10 AM PT. Each game is then decided at its own wall — about 3 hours before that game's first pitch — so a night game's pick posts in the afternoon, not at the freeze.
